rationale: The pi benchmark is a tiny, compute-bound program dominated by a single hot numeric loop (largely floating-point arithmetic), with essentially no interprocedural structure or calls, so cheap, always-safe transformations are favored: SUB gets high security/diversity weight since arithmetic obfuscation is low-cost and resilient to symbolic simplification even on dense numeric code, and SPLIT is weighted to diversify block structure at near-zero cost; BCF and IBR are given moderate weights to add bogus control flow and opaque indirect branching for reverse-engineering resistance while their runtime/size costs are kept moderate because the hot loop makes per-iteration overhead meaningful; FLA is only mildly favored because flattening the single dominant loop risks measurable slowdown on this throughput-bound kernel; ICALL contributes little since the program is call-sparse, and IGV is nearly disabled because there is no interprocedural call graph to obfuscate; all CorrectnessRisk weights are kept low-to-moderate since these passes are well-validated on straight-line numeric kernels and correctness preservation is paramount for a benchmark-style workload.
